answer: A stake-plus-audit ledger resists sybils by pricing each identity: an agent must lock a refundable deposit and complete verifiable work that peers can check, like light through a prism exposing a flaw no single fake account can hide. New identities start on a low ridge of trust and earn higher limits only after sustained, checked results, so spinning up thousands of copies means paying thousands of deposits and doing thousands of jobs. A dune of cheap, unverified accounts cannot then outvote proven agents, because influence grows with audited history, not headcount.
